n_a.text:
CONCEPT A — PATHWAY (recommended)

Idea: KGWF doesn't 'help people' — it opens doorways. The hero photograph sits inside an arch, a quiet nod to Jaipur's jharokhas and gateways, and a thin pathway line (Support → Skills → Confidence → Opportunity → Independence → Community impact) runs under the hero and returns in the impact section.

Feel: calm, editorial, institution-grade. Ivory ground, navy ink, sand only as hairlines and frames. Teal/sage appear only where the content is environmental or community-led.

Strongest at: credibility + warmth balance; scales cleanly to inner pages; least dependent on high-res photography (the arch crops tight).

Risk: the most restrained of the three — needs excellent photography to avoid feeling quiet.

Tweak: use the Tweaks button on the desktop board to swap the hero photograph.

n_b.text:
CONCEPT B — LEDGER

Idea: an annual-report / foundation aesthetic. Deep navy hero with a restrained serif headline (Source Serif 4), sand hairlines, a visible column system, and impact presented as a ledger with sources beside every number.

Feel: the most institutional and CSR-ready; reads well to corporate partners, auditors and government.

Strongest at: trust, transparency, the CSR conversion path and the Corporate / Learning vertical.

Risk: dark hero can feel formal; must keep community photography prominent so it doesn't drift toward a consultancy look.

The Support panel (right) shows the static donation experience: official UPI image unaltered, no gateway, no fake success state.

n_c.text:
CONCEPT C — FIELD NOTES

Idea: the website as a field journal. Photography leads; captions read like field notes (programme · place · [date]). The pathway becomes a numbered chapter rail that structures the whole homepage.

Feel: the warmest and most human. Sage and terracotta carry more of the page; navy anchors type and the footer.

Strongest at: storytelling, volunteer recruitment, social sharing.

Risk: highly dependent on large, high-resolution original photographs. The supplied community photos are 330–690px wide — at this scale they will look soft until originals are provided.
